intro: Since the end of communism, Poland has been one of Europe's biggest success stories, growing fast for three decades.

chapters.title: From shock therapy to boom
text: In 1990 Poland switched almost overnight from a planned economy to a market economy, a painful 'shock therapy' that was followed by years of strong growth. In 2009 it was the only EU country to avoid a recession.
Factories make cars, furniture, household appliances and parts for German companies, and big international firms run offices in Kraków and Wrocław. Poland is the EU's biggest apple grower.

chapters.title: Games and energy
text: CD Projekt, from Warsaw, created The Witcher games and Cyberpunk 2077, making Poland a major force in video games.
Coal still produces a large share of Poland's electricity, and the country is building wind farms and planning its first nuclear power station. It uses its own currency, the złoty, not the euro.

keyTerms.meaning: An economy run by the government, which decides what is made and at what price.
An economy where businesses and buyers decide what is made and prices.
